newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Monblan wins tender for 33 pct of Russia's Yukos.
newsitem.headline: Monblan wins tender for 33 pct of Russia's Yukos.

text.p: ZAO Monblan won an investment tender for a 33.3 percent stake in Russia's YUKOS oil company with a bid of $160.1 million, compared with a $160.0 million starting price, Menatep bank said on Monday.
Details of Monblan's ownership were not immediately clear but Menatep deputy chairman Konstantin Kagalovsky told reporters there was no connection between Menatep and Monblan.
Kagalovsky said a Moscow food factory made a second, lower bid. He was also head of the tender commission.
"YUKOS has become the first private oil company. The state has just 0.1 percent of the shares, which have not been sold at auctions," said Kagalovsky.
The stake was made up of 745.66 million shares and the winner will be obliged to invest $200 million in YUKOS over two years.
ZAO Laguna, a hitherto unknown company backed by Menatep, won the right to manage a 45 percent stake in YUKOS in the government's shares-for-loans scheme in December 1995.
The stake has since been diluted to 33.3 percent by a rights issue which raised YUKOS's authorised capital by 26 percent.
Laguna also won a further 33 percent in a separate investment tender last December.
The tender completed on Monday was the first time shares acquired under the scheme have been sold off.
Winners of the auctions have been free to sell the shares since September 1. Once the original loan is repaid, winners keep 30 percent of the proceeds while 70 percent goes into the state budget.
The shares-for-loans scheme proved highly controversial when several auctions were won by companies close to the organisers and at prices little more than the starting price.
YUKOS is one of Russia's biggest vertically integrated oil groups. Its main operating units are Yuganskneftegaz and Samaraneftegaz.
